title: Circuit Breaker Scenarios and Deploy Slice Matrix Sync
summary: Workshop-style sync to align deploy-slice matrix for upcoming 3-week ramp, agree circuit-breaker thresholds, rollback triggers, and ownership for staged degradation scenarios. Touched on KV cache eviction, quant-skew monitoring, and fast-fail playbooks. No final decisions on canary size; agreed to run two short bench runs and follow up.
topics: deploy slice matrix (traffic slicing, canary sizing)
KV cache eviction and prefix caching implications
quantization skew detection and metric alerts
transcript:
[00:00] Evan Cho: Alright, hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice. I want to call this a working workshop, so please interrupt. The agenda is the slice matrix + circuit-breaker thresholds for the next ramp.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Hi. Quick note — we only have 78 minutes, so I'd like to get to hard actions at the 60-minute mark.
[00:18] Jonas Reed: Sounds good. I'm mostly here for the risk criteria; we'll need sign-off from execs before any 50% canary.
[00:24] Samir Gupta: Yep, and SRE needs the fast-fail thresholds plainly defined otherwise teams will be paged at 3am.
[00:28] Lauren Kim: I'll share the current release matrix doc in chat — doc: https://intra.redwood/release/slice-matrix-draft (note: internal link).
[00:36] Evan Cho: Great, so start with the high level. We have three slices proposed: 1% pilot, 10% canary, 100% ramp with staged eviction tiers. The question is where to put the circuit-breaker bins.
[00:51] Marta Lopez: From infra we care about GPU saturation, tail-latency P95/P99, and error-rate spikes. Also KV cache miss amplification during partial rollouts — that bit keeps me up.
[01:04] Aisha Patel: Right, prefix-cache warmup is going to spike calls. We should pair the 10% canary with an explicit prefix-warmup step; otherwise latency will look bad but it's expected. Flag it as "warmup window" not an incident.
[01:18] Nick Zhao: Telemetry note — we need to distinguish warmup-induced latency from regressions. We'll add a warmup label to traces for the first 30m of a slice.
[01:27] Evan Cho: Ok, proposal: circuit-breaker categories: (A) Latency degradation (P95 +20% sustained for 5m), (B) Error rate (>1.5% of requests 5xx over 5m), (C) GPU OOMs or machine-level failures (any). Breaker actions vary by severity: warn -> pause rollout -> full rollback.
[01:46] Priya Singh: I'm worried about the 5m window; some noisy workloads will spike briefly. Can we do 2-of-3 buckets or require sustained for 10m for P99?
[01:56] Samir Gupta: Maybe split by metric: P95 can be 5m, P99 should be 10m and include error-rate corroboration. We don't want to roll back on transient network noise.
[02:07] Oliver Grant: Also include user-facing error signal — if synthetic transactions fail we should escalate faster.
[02:13] Evan Cho: Good point. Add a synthetic canary health check with shorter thresholds.
[02:18] Lauren Kim: I'll note that.
[02:20] Jonas Reed: For ownership, who flips the circuit-breaker? Is it automatic or manual?
[02:24] Samir Gupta: We want automatic pause for low-severity and auto-rollback only for catastrophic failures. Humans should confirm before any unpinning of models.
[02:33] Evan Cho: Ok so automated pause + paging on escalation. Manual explicit rollback only by release on-call.
[02:38] Priya Singh: On canary sizes: Ops suggests 10% is fine but product prefers smaller 5% for higher-risk models. Is there a hard reason for 10%?
[02:47] Marta Lopez: 10% gives better signal on latency percentiles without taking too much capacity. 5% often doesn't surface P99 shifts.
[02:56] Aisha Patel: But remember for some throttled customers, even 5% could show amplified cache misses. Maybe we do 5% early canary with extended warmup then a 20% short canary for latency signal.
[03:10] Evan Cho: So proposed matrix: Pilot 1% (smoke), Canary Stage A 5% with 60m warmup, Canary Stage B 20% with 15m warmup, Ramp to 100% with staggered eviction tiers.
[03:25] Nick Zhao: Telemetry can do the warmup tag and create a dashboard to collapse warmup windows. We'll need graph templates.
[03:31] Samir Gupta: On rollback triggers, we also need to take into account quant-skew. If quantized model produces a shift in top-1 token distribution or embedding drift > threshold, that should be an immediate alert.
[03:44] Priya Singh: How do we detect quant-skew automatically? We have sample evals but they're not run online today.
[03:50] Lauren Kim: We can run lightweight embeddings on a sampled prefix set and compute cosine drift. It's a small compute overhead.
[03:56] Aisha Patel: Set a provisional threshold: drift > 0.07 average cosine over sample -> escalate. We can refine after bench runs.
[04:06] Jonas Reed: Put that into the runbook as "Quantization drift check".
[04:10] Evan Cho: Good. Now I want to go through a couple of failure scenarios to ensure ownership and messaging are clear. Scenario 1: P95 jumps 40% at 20% canary while synthetic checks pass. What happens?
[04:25] Samir Gupta: If synthetics pass but P95 jumps, likely cache warmup or tail scheduler. SRE to investigate KV miss rate and evictions. If it's warmup, document and continue; if not, pause rollout.
[04:36] Priya Singh: Who makes the call? SRE runs triage and then release engineer decides to pause or continue.
[04:42] Lauren Kim: I'll be the release decision authority in this example.
[04:44] Evan Cho: OK. Scenario 2: sudden increase in 5xxs by 2% at 5% pilot. Rollback?
[04:52] Samir Gupta: 2% 5xx sustained over 5m meets error-rate breaker — auto-pause and page SRE. If multiple hosts failing or OOMs, trigger immediate rollback.
[05:02] Marta Lopez: And we should have an automated tag on traces to help root cause across pod restarts.
[05:08] Nick Zhao: We'll add span tag 'slice' to synthetic traces and user traces during rollout.
[05:14] Evan Cho: Good. Scenario 3: model quality regression detected by customer feedback or eval set shift.
[05:21] Aisha Patel: We'll have evaluation prompts run in shadow and compare perplexity / regen difference. If quality drop > X we pause. Need to choose X.
[05:29] Priya Singh: Suggest threshold: 5% drop in eval pass rate across critical prompt set. It's arbitrary; bench runs will calibrate.
[05:36] Jonas Reed: Also, legal/security wants audit logs of who approved rollouts and rollbacks. Renee, anything else?
[05:42] Renee Park: Yes, SSO and audit trails are required. Also we need to log any manual override and the reason. That goes into compliance docs.
[05:50] Evan Cho: Noted. Lauren and Renee will sync after this.
[05:54] Lauren Kim: Yep.
[05:55] Evan Cho: Quick tangent: KV cache eviction strategy — Priya?
[05:59] Priya Singh: If we do staged eviction we need eviction tiers per slice. Tier 0 for pilot, tier 1 for canary, etc. Eviction timing should be coordinated with warmup window to avoid double penalty.
[06:10] Samir Gupta: Also need to monitor miss amplification — if miss rate increases by >200% during rollout we hit an alert. Might need temporary extra cache capacity.
[06:19] Aisha Patel: Could we pre-warm top prefixes in pilot? Maybe run a prefetch job that simulates traffic on model prefixes selected from heavy users.
[06:27] Nick Zhao: We can do that; it's a background job that hits the model with anonymized tokens. We'll need to mask PII though.
[06:33] Evan Cho: Security note — ensure pre-warm doesn't leak customer data; use synthetic anonymized prompts.
[06:38] Marta Lopez: Capacity — for the larger 20% canary, ops wants a safety pool of 10% extra GPUs to absorb slowdowns. Budget?
[06:47] Jonas Reed: We'll provision on-call budget but need to quantify expected spend. Samir, can you estimate?
[06:52] Samir Gupta: Rough order: extra 10% GPUs for 3 hours during canary ramp -> estimate $Xk. I'll put numbers in the follow-up.
[06:59] Evan Cho: Good. Next, communication plan: avoid posting warmup alerts to general channel. We'll have a rollout-status channel where synthesis posts warmup vs incident.
[07:09] Oliver Grant: I'll create channel #rollout-x so it's specific per release. Also we need an email summary for execs on decision points.
[07:16] Evan Cho: Ok. Time to capture concrete action items. But before that, any objections to the matrix?
[07:22] Priya Singh: One ask — add an explicit "no-traffic-increase" guard for the first 15m after a stage change to allow steady-state monitoring.
[07:30] Samir Gupta: That makes sense. We'll hold traffic increases until warmup label expires.
[07:35] Lauren Kim: Also add a metric to detect quant-skew and a dedicated dashboard link. I'll create the dashboard template.
[07:43] Evan Cho: Great. Anything else?
[07:46] Jonas Reed: Need to run two bench runs: one with 5% canary + warmup and one with 20% to calibrate P99. Schedule tomorrow and Friday?
[07:54] Priya Singh: Tomorrow morning for the 5% smoke, Friday for 20% ramp.
[07:58] Evan Cho: Alright, closing. We'll capture action items and reconvene Monday to review bench results. Thanks everyone.
[08:05] (crosstalk) multiple: thanks, bye.
next_steps: Run bench run 1: 5% canary + 60m warmup — schedule tomorrow morning
Run bench run 2: 20% canary + 15m warmup — schedule Friday
Release engineer to create rollout-status channel and dashboard templates
Security to confirm pre-warm masking approach and audit logging requirements
SRE to estimate cost for 10% spare GPU safety pool and document in follow-up
